2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, is as follows:

On 01.07.2018 at about 6.50 a.m., the deceased Sri.
Dinesh E. was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA- 41-EJ-6204 along with pillion rider Shafi and when they were going from Electronic City side to Koodlu gate on Hosur Main road in front of Singsandra Bharath Petrol Bunk, at that time, when they were going behind one unknown lorry all of a sudden another lorry
bearing

Reg. 
No. KA-51-D-6657 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-51-EJ- 6204 to the back side and rear right side portion of the motor cycle and due to the impact, motor cycle rider as well as pillion rider fell down and dragged some distance along with the motor cycle and rider as well as pillion  SCCH-17 5 MVC 1391/2019 rider sustained grievous injuries to head.
The injured Dinesh was shifted to Blossom Hospital, but he succumbed to the said injuries.
The petitioners have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral death ceremonies and other expenses.
The deceased was working as mason and earning Rs.24,000/- per month and he was contributing his entire income to his family.
Due to the untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered Shruthi vs Ashok Kumar.N on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102312911/

The petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 & 3 are the children and petitioner No.4 & 5 are the parents of the deceased Dinesh, have lost their beloved care taker.
The respondents are the owner, insured and insurer of the offending lorry are jointly severally liable to pay the  SCCH-17 6 MVC 1391/2019 compensation to the petitioners.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, all the respondents appeared through their respective advocates.
The respondent No.1 and 3 have filed their written statements separately.
The respondent No.2 has not filed written statement.

The respondent No.1 owner in the written statement has contended that on the date of the alleged accident the driver of the 1st respondent's lorry bearing No.KA-51-D- 6657 was driven by its driver slowly.

The deceased was riding the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner,
without observing the traffic rules.
This lorry has insured with 3rd respondent which was in force as on the date of the accident.
The petitioner's vehicle also involved in the accident.

Further contended that, the accident was  SCCH-17 7 MVC 1391/2019 Shruthi vs Ashok Kumar.N on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102312911/

Further contended that at the time of accident the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license.

It is further contended that the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased himself as he was riding the motor cycle without keeping proper distance and dashed against the back side portion of the  SCCH-17 8 MVC 1391/2019 lorry.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence the respondent No.3 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

On going through the documents, one Ravikumara, who is working as police constable at Hulimavu Traffic police station has lodged the complaint on 01.07.2018 by alleging the accident within the limits of their police station.
On the basis of Ex.P1 first information FIR is registered on the very same day.

As per the Ex.P1 first information on 1.7.2018 at about 7.15 AM., while the complainant discharging his duty as a police constable, received an information from the police control room that an accident has taken place in front of Bharath Petrol Bunk at Hosur main road and he was instructed to go and see that place as such, immediately the informant went to the place of accident and saw the accident.
In that place the damaged Pulsar motor cycle was found on the road.

The pillion rider also sustained minor injuries.
Immediately after the accident,the injureds were shifted to Blossom Hospital.
The alleged offending vehicles went away.

After enquiry the complainant went to the blossom hospital and saw the injured persons in which the deceased Dinesh was not in a position to speak, hence the complainant enquired the pillion rider Shafi R. who gave the information about the accident.

Due to this impact the rider of the motor cycle sustained injuries and thereafter both the injured were shifted to Blossom Hospital, but the injured Dinesh died in the hospital.

31. Liability:
Admittedly, the respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner, insured and insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.3 in its objection statement admitted the issuance of insurance policy to the tipper bearing Reg. No. KA-51-D-6657.
The 3rd respondent has issued notice calling up on the 1st respondent to furnish the DL of the driver who drove the vehicle as on the date of he accident.
The respondent No.1 who is also the Manager of the respondent No.2 firm examined himself as RW.3 and produced Ex.R8- driving licence extract.
As per  SCCH-17 26 MVC 1391/2019 this document the driver of truck bearing No. KA51-D- 6657 was having driving licence to drive the same.
As per Ex.R8 the driver i.e., Virupaksha Malakanawar was having valid DL to drive the transportation vehicle from 17.10.2017 to 16.10.2020.
The date of accident is 1.7.2018.
hence, as per these document the driver of tuck bearing No. KA-51-D-6657 was having valid driving licence to drive the same.
Ex.P7 is the head of charge sheet wherein the said Virupaksha Malakannawar was shown as accused.
In the charge sheet only offence under Shruthi vs Ashok Kumar.N on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102312911/
17 Sec. 279, 337 & 304(A) are invoked by the IO and no offence are invoked by alleging the driving of the truck by its driver without having DL.
Hence, it has to be considered that driver of the offending vehicle was holding the driving licence.

Accordingly the respondent No. 1 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the  SCCH-17 27 MVC 1391/2019 compensation to the petitioners and the respondent No.3 insurance company shall indemnify the liability of respondent No.1 & 2.
The petitioners are entitle for the compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
Accordingly Issue No.4 answered partly in the affirmative.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.28,65,000/- (Rupees Twenty eight lakhs sixty five thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioner Nos.1 to 5 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 50:15:15:10:10.
The respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of amount awarded to Petitioner No.1, 50% shall be released on her proper identification and remaining 50% to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in her name.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The issue No.1 is casted by putting the burden on the petitioners to show that the deceased Dinesh was died due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and the issue No.2 is casted the burden on the petitioners to prove the alleged negligence.
During the course of evidence the original Aadhaar cards are compared with the notarized copies,
found correct and returned the same to the petitioners.
The respondents do not dispute the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
22. In the claim petition, strict proof of relationship is not necessary like in civil suit.
The respondents also not adduced contra evidence.
Considering the documentary  SCCH-17 20 MVC 1391/2019 and oral evidence there are sufficient material to show that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 & 3 are the minor children and petitioner No.4 & 5 are the parents of the deceased are the dependents of deceased.
24 . In the petition it is alleged that the deceased was working as mason and earning Rs.24,000/- per month.
In this regard, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
In the absence of proof of income it cannot be considered that, the deceased was earning Rs.24,000/- per month.
Hence, the notional income of the deceased was Rs.12,500/- in the year-2018, then the annual income comes to Rs.1,50,000/-.
17 Sec. 279, 337 & 304(A) are invoked by the IO and no offence are invoked by alleging the driving of the truck by its driver without having DL.
Hence, it has to be considered that driver of the offending vehicle was holding the driving licence.
opennyai_summary.decision:
As per the above decision, 40% of notional income should be added to total loss of dependency, to the age of deceased, which will be Rs.7,20,000/-.
Hence I inclined to award a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium to the petitioners, Rs.25,000/- each towards loss of love and affection.
Further, I inclined to award compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.5,000/-
towards transportation of dead body.
Accordingly the respondent No. 1 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the  SCCH-17 27 MVC 1391/2019 compensation to the petitioners and the respondent No.3 insurance company shall indemnify the liability of respondent No.1 & 2.
The petitioners are entitle for the compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
Accordingly Issue No.4 answered partly in the affirmative.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.28,65,000/- (Rupees Twenty eight lakhs sixty five thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioner Nos.1 to 5 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 50:15:15:10:10.
The respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Out of amount awarded to Petitioner No.1, 50% shall be released on her proper identification and remaining 50% to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in her name.
The entire compensation amount awarded to petitioner No.2 & 3 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in their name in any Scheduled Bank, till they attains the age of majority.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to respondent No.4 & 5, it is ordered to release the entire amount to them.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
